theme: Unit 17 review, The New Covenant Inaugurated, John
memoryText: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Jesus says this to Nicodemus in the night, and it has become the best known verse in the Bible. Every word carries weight.

“For God.” The subject of the sentence is God. Salvation begins with him, not us.

“So loved.” The word “so” means “in this way.” This is how God loved: by giving. His love is not a feeling alone. It acts, at great cost.

“The world.” Not just Israel, not just the good. The whole sinful, rebellious world. If God loved the world, he loves you.

“That he gave his only Son.” The Father gave the Son he loved from all eternity. This is the gift of the cross, the greatest gift in history.

“That whoever believes in him.” The way to receive the gift is belief, trust in Jesus. “Whoever” means anyone, with no exceptions.

“Should not perish but have eternal life.” Two destinies: perishing or life. Eternal life begins now, in knowing God, and lasts forever.

When you doubt whether God cares about you, say this verse. It is the gospel in a sentence.
unitRecap: You have read the whole Gospel of John, which was written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and by believing have life in his name. It began in eternity with the Word, who was with God and was God, and who became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth. Through seven signs and seven “I AM” statements, John showed who Jesus is: the bread of life, the light of the world, the door, the good shepherd, the resurrection and the life, the way, the truth, and the life, and the true vine. Jesus told Nicodemus that he must be born again, offered living water to a Samaritan woman, healed a blind man, and raised Lazarus. He said “Before Abraham was, I am,” and “I and the Father are one.” In the Upper Room he washed his disciples’ feet, gave a new commandment, and promised the Holy Spirit, the Helper who would be with them forever. He taught them to abide in the vine and prayed for all who would believe through their word. He was arrested, tried, and crucified, saying “It is finished,” and was raised on the third day. He called Mary by name, drew Thomas from doubt to worship, and restored Peter. Along the way you doctrinally paused on the incarnation, regeneration, and worship, and prayed through Psalms 36, 139, 119, 43, 23, 100, and 103, which gave voice to the light, the shepherd, and the steadfast love at the heart of this Gospel.

reviewQuestions.question: What does the Prologue teach about the identity of Jesus?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Reread John 1:1-18. Notice what it says about the Word’s relationship to God, to creation, and to us. Write a few sentences about why it matters that Jesus is both fully God and fully human.

reviewQuestions.question: What do the seven “I AM” statements reveal about who Jesus is?
reviewQuestions.prompt: List them: the bread of life (6:35), the light of the world (8:12), the door (10:9), the good shepherd (10:11), the resurrection and the life (11:25), the way, the truth, and the life (14:6), and the true vine (15:1). Choose the one that speaks most to your need right now and say why.

reviewQuestions.question: What does the Upper Room Discourse teach about the Holy Spirit?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Look at John 14:16-26, 15:26-27, and 16:7-15. What does the Spirit do for believers and for the world? Why did Jesus say it was to their advantage that he go away?

reviewQuestions.question: What does “abiding in the vine” look like in everyday Christian life?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Reread John 15:1-17. Think about concrete practices of abiding, such as prayer, Scripture, obedience, and fellowship. Describe one change you could make this week to stay more connected to Christ.

prayerPrompts: Thank God for loving the world so much that he gave his Son.
Thank him for what John has shown you of Jesus.
Ask him to keep the unit verse before you.
